Cut the pages by a row budget

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_paginate_rows.Rd

plan_paginate_rows() is the row axis of pagination: how many body rows a page holds and what a page break may cut — a group kept whole, or cut with a continuation label. With page_by the body is first partitioned by the value of a column (a period, a cohort), each value a page named after it, and the row budget applies within one partition. A page per value with no row budget is plan_paginate_group(); the column axis is plan_paginate_cols().

Usage

plan_paginate_rows(
  .plan,
  max_rows = NULL,
  split = NULL,
  break_before = NULL,
  min_group_rows = NULL,
  cont_label = NULL,
  page_by = NULL,
  heading = NULL,
  heading_at = NULL,
  na_label = NULL
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

max_rows

The most body rows a page holds, for the "group_safe" and "group_force" splits (which need it). Given with the split left out, the split is "group_safe" (a listing's is left to as_rtftables(), which does the same on its record column); with a split that has no row budget ("none", "rows", a page per value) it stops. Blank rows count only with plan_blanks(counted = TRUE).

split

How a page break is placed, as_rtftables(split = ):

"none"

one page; the default when max_rows is not given (with max_rows alone the default is "group_safe"). Written out with max_rows it stops: the budget would have nothing to cut.

"group_safe"

whole groups to a page: a group that does not fit starts the next page; one longer than a page is cut, with a continuation label.

"group_force"

a cut every max_rows rows wherever it falls, a group straddling it continued on the next page; only min_group_rows pulls a cut back.

"rows"

a cut before each row of break_before.

a function

a split of your own, as as_rtftables() takes it.

break_before

With split = "rows": the row positions to cut before, as_rtftables(split_rows = ).

min_group_rows

Widow / orphan control, as_rtftables(min_group_rows = ) (default 2; 0 turns it off). A group that starts on a page with fewer than this many rows after its first row (its heading, in a value-grouped column the row that opens the group) moves whole to the next page; a cut inside a group is pulled back so at least this many of its rows go on to the next page.

cont_label

The text added to a group's heading on the page it is continued on, as_rtftables(cont_label = ).

page_by

The column(s) whose value partitions the body first, each value a page named after it, as_rtftables(page_by = ); the settings above then apply within one partition. The BY column is printed unless hidden (plan_hide()); it is a page key, never a row group.

heading, heading_at

With page_by: the BY page's name as a template and where it prints, as plan_paginate_group()'s. With one page_by column {value} is its value; with several the heading carries a token for each column by its name, "Analyte: {ANALYTE}", and no {value}.

na_label

With page_by: the text a blank BY value ("" or NA) prints as in the page's heading ({value}, a {<column>}) and in its name. The default NULL is the empty text, so a template "Severity: {value}" prints "Severity: ". Like cont_label, a text of the page, and like na, the text of a missing value.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; as_rtftables() for the splits in full.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

# Invented records of twelve subjects
subj <- data.frame(Subject = sprintf("01-%03d", 1:12),
                   Age = c(61, 58, 70, 66, 54, 49, 73, 62, 68, 57, 60, 71))

# Minimal: five rows a page
pages <- table_plan(subj) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 5, split = "group_force") |>
  plan_apply()
vapply(pages, function(pg) nrow(pg$data), integer(1))
#> [1] 5 5 2

# A laboratory value over two periods: a page per period, each named
# after it, cut every two rows; the period itself is not printed
lab <- data.frame(
  Period  = rep(c("Period 1", "Period 2"), each = 4),
  Subject = rep(sprintf("01-%03d", 1:4), 2),
  ALT     = c(22, 25, 31, 19, 24, 27, 29, 20))
pages <- table_plan(lab) |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 2, split = "group_force",
                     page_by = "Period", heading = "{value}",
                     heading_at = "title") |>
  plan_hide("Period") |>
  plan_apply()
length(pages)
#> [1] 4
pages[[2]]
#> ────────────
#> Subject  ALT
#> ────────────
#> 01-003   31 
#> 01-004   19 
#> 
#> <rtftable> 2 rows x 2 columns
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>
